user.title: SmartHus
user.description: Smart control of solar, battery, EV charger and heat pump based on electricity prices. Devices are added afterwards under Configure.

prices.title: Electricity price and tariffs
prices.description: Choose Strømligning if the Strømligning integration is installed. The actual price from the customer's plan is then used, and the tariffs below are only a fallback. Otherwise SmartHus calculates the price from the Energi Data Service spot price and the tariffs below (DKK/kWh excl. VAT, winter = October–March). The sale price is the spot price (from Strømligning, otherwise Energi Data Service) minus the sale deduction, excl. VAT.

data.price_source: Where does the electricity price come from?
data.stromligning_spot_entity: Strømligning: spot price sensor (for the sale price)
data.include_vat: Add 25% VAT to the purchase price

data_description.price_source: Strømligning gives the actual price from the customer's plan. Otherwise SmartHus calculates it from the spot price and the tariffs below.

data_description.include_vat: Turn on for private customers (25% VAT).
data_description.energinet_tariff: Energinet grid + system tariff per kWh excl. VAT.
data_description.elafgift: Electricity tax per kWh excl. VAT.
data_description.tariff_winter_low: Your grid company's tariff excl. VAT, Oct–Mar 00–06.
data_description.stromligning_price_vat: Choose whether the price sensor (and the tomorrow sensor) shows prices including or excluding VAT. Without VAT, SmartHus adds 25 % VAT so all prices and savings include VAT.
data_description.stromligning_spot_vat: Choose whether the spot price sensor includes VAT. The sale price for solar power is always without VAT.

battery.title: Battery / inverter
battery.description: Choose one: A) drop-down (SigEnergy, FoxESS, SolaX), B) Huawei – just pick the battery, or C) scripts for other brands.

data.battery_option_charge: A) Mode name: charge from grid
data.battery_script_charge: C) Script: charge battery from grid
data.battery_power_sensor: Battery power right now (W or kW) – optional
data.battery_power_sign: What does a positive battery value mean?

data_description.house_energy_sensor: Increasing energy meter (kWh) of the house consumption – e.g. from the inverter ('Load consumption total'), a P1 meter or an electricity meter. Every night SmartHus learns the hourly consumption from the last 14 days (weekdays and weekends separately) and keeps enough in the battery for the house until power is cheap again. Only the surplus is sold. Requires long-term statistics. The reserve is used after 2 days of history.
data_description.battery_mode_entity: A select entity that switches the inverter's mode. Leave empty if you use scripts.
data_description.battery_option_charge: Exactly as shown in the drop-down, e.g. SigEnergy: Command Charging (Grid First).
data_description.battery_script_charge: Runs when the battery should charge from the grid. Variables: smarthus_state, price, sale_price, min_soc, max_soc.
data_description.battery_script_discharge: Runs when the battery should discharge in expensive hours.
data_description.battery_script_normal: Runs when returning to normal operation, also when control is turned off. Always set it when using scripts.
data_description.battery_charge_energy_sensor: Increasing meter (kWh) of all energy charged into the battery. Only used for savings.
data_description.battery_discharge_energy_sensor: Increasing meter (kWh) of all energy delivered by the battery. Only used for savings.
data_description.battery_huawei_device: With the Huawei Solar integration, just pick the battery here – SmartHus handles forced charge/discharge itself. No scripts needed.
data_description.battery_huawei_power: Power used for forced charge/discharge. Default 5000 W.
data_description.battery_power_sensor: Only used for the energy flow at the top of the card.
data_description.battery_power_sign: Huawei and SigEnergy usually show charging as positive.
data_description.battery_option_sell_solar: Optional. A mode where solar power is exported and the battery is not charged by the panels. SmartHus then sells solar when the sale price beats charging cheaply from the grid later. Only used when the battery already holds the house reserve. Leave empty to disable.
data_description.battery_script_sell_solar: Optional. Runs when solar should be sold instead of charging the battery (e.g. set max charge power to 0). The normal script runs afterwards.

solar.title: Solar
solar.description: Used for the solar overview and to stop export when the sale price is below your limit ('Stop export below' on the card). Stopping export can be done with a switch (on = stop), a drop-down (two option names), a number such as an export limit (two values) or two scripts.

data.solar_curtail_entity: Stop export: switch, drop-down or number
data.solar_forecast_sensor: Solar forecast: remaining production today (kWh) – optional
data.export_value_stop: Number: value when export is stopped
data.grid_power_sensor: Grid power right now (W or kW) – optional
data.grid_power_sign: What does a positive value mean?
data.solar_power_sensor: Solar production right now (W or kW) – optional

data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Makes the battery reserve more accurate by subtracting expected solar. Solcast: sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_remaining_today. Forecast.Solar: sensor.energy_production_today_remaining. Without a forecast, solar is assumed not to cover any house consumption – the cautious choice.
data_description.solar_curtail_entity: The entity that stops grid export. Leave empty if you use scripts.
data_description.export_option_stop: Only for a drop-down, e.g. 'Zero Export'.
data_description.export_option_normal: Only for a drop-down, e.g. 'Selling First'.
data_description.export_value_normal: Only for a number, e.g. the inverter's max power in W.
data_description.export_script_stop: Runs when the sale price drops below the limit. Use together with 'start export again'.
data_description.export_script_start: Runs when the sale price is above the limit again, and when control is turned off.
data_description.solar_energy_sensor: Increasing meter (kWh) of all solar production.
data_description.grid_export_energy_sensor: Increasing meter (kWh) of all energy exported to the grid.
data_description.grid_power_sensor: Used for solar surplus (hot water and EV). A power sensor showing export/import right now.
data_description.grid_power_sign: Many inverters show export as positive; P1 meters often show import as positive.
data_description.solar_power_sensor: Current solar power. EV solar charging starts when production is above 'Start at solar above'. Without it, export is used.
data_description.grid_import_energy_sensor: Increasing meter (kWh) of all energy bought from the grid, e.g. from a P1 meter. The card then shows how much you bought, what it cost and your average price.
data_description.solar_investment: What the solar system cost in total incl. installation. Used to show how much of the system has been paid back (ROI) and when it will be paid back.

ev.title: EVs
ev.description: Choose an EV to edit it, or add a new one. Tick 'Remove' to delete the selected car.

hotwater.title: Hot water
hotwater.description: A switch is turned on in the cheapest continuous period of the day. For a water_heater or climate entity the temperature is raised instead.

data.hotwater_min_temp_entity: Heat pump's lower hot water limit (°C) – optional

data_description.hotwater_entity: What SmartHus uses to heat the water in the cheapest period: • the heat pump's own hot water function, e.g. a switch or button such as 'Charge' or 'Hot water boost' • a switch/relay for the heating element, e.g. a Shelly • a water_heater/climate entity – then the temperature is set instead. A button is pressed once when heating should start, and the heat pump stops by itself.
data_description.hotwater_energy_sensor: Increasing meter (kWh) for hot water. Only used for savings. If one heat pump does both heating and hot water, select the same meter here and under Heating – consumption then counts as hot water while SmartHus heats water and as heating otherwise. It is only counted once.
data_description.hotwater_temp_sensor: Measures the water temperature. With a sensor, SmartHus turns the switch off when the water reaches the max. temperature and on again in the cheap period if it has cooled 3 °C.
data_description.hotwater_min_temp_entity: The heat pump's own set point for when it reheats the water, e.g. 'Hot water target temperature'. Used as 'Lowest temperature' for on-demand hot water. If not selected, the value on the card is used.

heating.title: Heating / heat pump
heating.description: The temperature is raised in the cheapest hours and lowered in the most expensive.

data_description.heating_climate_entity: The thermostat or heat pump (climate entity) raised in cheap hours and lowered in expensive hours.
data_description.heatpump_energy_sensor: Increasing meter (kWh) of the heat pump. Only used for savings.

weather.title: Weather and outdoor temperature
weather.description: Used for the weather and outdoor temperature in the energy flow on the card and for the heating limit ('Active below outdoor temperature'). Both are optional – if empty, SmartHus uses Home Assistant's own weather from the cloud (Met.no 'Home').

data_description.outdoor_temp_sensor: Your own outdoor sensor. Used when available; otherwise the temperature from the weather entity is used.
data_description.weather_entity: The weather entity for the weather picture (sun, clouds, rain, snow …) and the outdoor temperature if you have no sensor. If empty, Home Assistant's own is found automatically (weather.forecast_home).

ev_car.title: EV: {car}
ev_car.description: The charger is enabled in the cheapest hours before the car's ready time. With the car's battery level (SoC) selected, it only charges to the target SoC.

data.ev_plug_sensor: Charging cable connected (from the car) – optional
data.ev_power_sensor: Charging power right now (W or kW) – optional

data_description.car_name: Shown on the card and in entity names.
data_description.ev_charger_entity: The switch that allows or stops charging, e.g. Easee switch.easee_is_enabled.
data_description.ev_soc_sensor: The car's battery level in % from the car's own integration. With SoC it only charges to the target SoC.
data_description.ev_energy_sensor: Increasing meter (kWh) of all energy the charger has delivered, e.g. Easee 'Lifetime energy'. ONLY used to calculate savings; control works without it.
data_description.ev_current_entity: For other chargers with a number entity for the current in amps, e.g. Zaptec 'Available current'.
data_description.ev_current_script: Only for chargers that are neither Easee nor have a number entity. The script gets 'current' (A).
data_description.ev_easee_device: For an Easee charger: pick it here and SmartHus controls the current without a script.
data_description.ev_plug_sensor: Sensor from the car's integration showing if the cable is plugged in. With several cars on one charger, SmartHus only controls the connected car. Without it, pick the connected car on the card.
data_description.ev_power_sensor: The charger's current power, e.g. Easee sensor.[charger]_power. Used for the energy flow.

import_solar_history.name: Import solar history
import_solar_history.description: Rebuilds solar production, self-consumption, export and grid import hour by hour from Home Assistant's long-term statistics and the actual electricity price for each hour. Safe to run again – the figures are rebuilt from scratch.

start_date.name: Start date
start_date.description: First day to include. Empty = as far back as history goes.

rebuild_energy_overview.name: Rebuild energy overview
rebuild_energy_overview.description: Rebuilds the energy overview (consumption, purchase and sale per device) from scratch using Home Assistant's long-term statistics and the actual price for each hour.
